title: Overview
text: Documentation Pi-Bolt documentation Pi-Bolt is the Pi coding agent compiled ahead of time to native code. It is the Pi you already use, with the same commands, sessions, settings, providers and extensions, as one executable that starts two to three times sooner than Pi on Bun and uses about a third of its CPU. title: Overview
text: Pi is a TypeScript program. Stock Pi runs on Bun or Node, which parse its code at every launch and compile the hot parts with a just-in-time (JIT) compiler while it runs. Pi-Bolt compiles every function of Pi to machine code when the executable is built, and stores Pi's modules already loaded. At launch there is nothing to parse and nothing to warm up. What stays the same: Your configuration. Pi-Bolt reads ~/.pi/agent : your providers and logins, settings, sessions, skills, prompt templates and extensions. Pi's behavior. title: Installation
text: Get started Installation Install Pi-Bolt with one command. The installer downloads the release for your system, checks its checksum and signature, and puts pi-bolt on your PATH. It does not change your Pi installation.

title: Installation
text: macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon. There is no build for Intel Macs. Linux on x86-64 with glibc 2.17 or later. musl distributions such as Alpine are not supported. Windows 10 (1809) or later, or Windows 11, on x64. Pi-Bolt does not need Node.js, Bun or Pi. npm is only needed if you install with npm.

Platform PIBOLT_VARIANT Build macOS arm64 Default macOS arm64-jit JIT on, for heavy run-time extensions Linux x64 Default, for CPUs with AVX2 (Intel Haswell, AMD Zen and later) Linux x64-baseline Any x86-64 CPU. title: Installation
text: $ pi-bolt --version 1.1.0 (Pi-Bolt 0.8.0, darwin-arm64, JIT off) The first number is the Pi release this build is made from. The rest is the Pi-Bolt release, the platform, and whether the JIT is on. To check that Pi runs its compiled code, see Check the compiled code .

title: Installation
text: $ pi-bolt update # Pi-Bolt only $ pi-bolt update --all # Pi-Bolt and your extensions With npm, run npm update -g pi-bolt ; the next run downloads the new release. Running the installer again also updates.

title: Installation
text: Run the installer again and choose uninstall . It removes the Pi-Bolt builds from ~/.pi-bolt and the pi-bolt link. With npm, run npm uninstall -g pi-bolt , then delete ~/.pi-bolt/npm , where the npm package keeps the release it downloaded. Your Pi configuration in ~/.pi/agent belongs to Pi and is not removed.

title: Installation
text: Download a build from the latest release , check it against SHA256SUMS , unpack it, and run ./pi (on Windows, pi-bolt.exe ). Keep the unpacked folder together: the executable uses the files around it for themes, HTML export and image tools. Link to the executable rather than copying it. Download For pi-bolt-darwin-arm64.tar.xz macOS on Apple silicon pi-bolt-linux-x64.tar.xz Linux, CPUs with AVX2 pi-bolt-linux-x64-baseline.tar.xz Linux, any x86-64 CPU pi-bolt-win32-x64.zip Windows x64 The JIT builds are pi-bolt-darwin-arm64-jit.tar.xz , pi-bolt-linux-x64-jit.tar.xz and pi-bolt-win32-x64-jit.zip

title: Installation
text: Set these in the environment of the installer: curl ... | NAME=value sh on macOS and Linux, $env:NAME = "value" before the command on Windows. title: Quickstart

Install Pi-Bolt $ curl -fsSL https://pi-bolt.opensec.in/install.sh | sh On Windows or with npm, see Installation . Start it in a project $ cd my-project $ pi-bolt Pi-Bolt opens Pi's terminal interface in the current folder. That folder is what the agent reads and edits. Connect a model If you have used Pi, your providers and logins are already there. Otherwise type /login and pick a provider, or set a provid

title: Quickstart
text: $ pi-bolt "Explain the build setup" # start with a prompt $ pi-bolt -p "List the TODOs in src/" # run one prompt, print the answer, exit $ pi-bolt -c # continue the last session here $ pi-bolt -r # pick a session to resume $ pi-bolt --model sonnet:high # a model, with a thinking level $ pi-bolt @README.md "Summarize this" # include a file pi-bolt --help lists every option. They are Pi's options; Pi's CLI reference describes them in full.

title: Quickstart
text: Pi-Bolt and Pi share ~/.pi/agent , so both see the same: providers, logins and API keys ( auth.json , models.json ); settings ( settings.json ); sessions, which either can resume; extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes. Install an extension with either command and both load it: $ pi-bolt install npm:opensec-pi-todo A tool that starts Pi by running pi keeps using stock Pi. To make it use Pi-Bolt, point it at pi-bolt : see Integrations .

title: Choose a build
text: Guides Choose a build Every platform has two builds. Pi itself is compiled ahead of time in both. They differ in what happens to code that is loaded while Pi runs, such as extensions.

title: Choose a build
text: Default (JIT off) JIT build (JIT on) Pi's own code Compiled machine code Compiled machine code Extensions loaded at run time Interpreted Interpreted, then JIT-compiled as they warm up bun:ffi , heavy eval / new Function bun:ffi does not work Works Memory Lowest Higher once the JIT has compiled something pi-bolt --version ends in JIT off JIT on A JIT (just-in-time compiler) turns code into machine code while the program runs. Pi-Bolt's default build has none: Pi was compiled before you ran it, so it does not need one, and it saves the JIT's compiler threads, warm-up and memory.

title: Choose a build
text: No extensions, or light ones (a todo list, UI panels, small hooks, most extensions): the default build. These spend their time waiting on the model, files or processes, so how their code runs does not show. Extensions that do heavy work in JavaScript (search, parsing, analysis over many files): the JIT build. On the default build their code is interpreted. Extensions that use bun:ffi , such as pi-fff: the JIT build. On the default build they fail with bun:ffi requires the JIT , because native calls through bun:ffi are generated by the JIT. title: Extensions
text: Guides Extensions Pi extensions and Pi packages work in Pi-Bolt without changes. They are found, installed and configured exactly as in Pi. What differs is how their code runs, which depends on the build.

title: Extensions
text: Pi-Bolt loads extensions from the same places as Pi: ~/.pi/agent/extensions , a project's .pi/extensions , Pi packages, and -e <path> on the command line. $ pi-bolt install npm:opensec-pi-todo # install a Pi package $ pi-bolt list # list installed packages $ pi-bolt update --extensions # update them $ pi-bolt remove npm:opensec-pi-todo # remove one $ pi-bolt config # turn resources on and off Pi-Bolt installs packages with its own package manager when npm is not installed. A run-time extension's own dependencies resolve as they do on Node, through its package.json . Writing extensions is cover

title: Extensions
section: Extensions that need the JIT build
text: Extensions that call native libraries through bun:ffi fail on the default build with bun:ffi requires the JIT . An example is pi-fff , which replaces Pi's find and grep with FFF, a fast, pre-indexed file search in Rust. Extensions that run a lot of code they generate with eval , new Function or vm : that code is only ever interpreted on the default build. Extensions that do heavy work in JavaScript : they work on the default build, more slowly. Install the JIT build with PIBOLT_VARIANT , as described in Switch builds .

title: Extensions
text: Some extensions start more Pi processes, for example to run subagents. If such an extension runs the pi command, its subagents run on stock Pi (or fail when Pi is not installed). Check the extension's settings for the command it runs. For pi-subagents , set: export PI_SUBAGENT_PI_BINARY=pi-bolt

title: Extensions
text: The installer offers two extensions that OpenSec maintains for Pi-Bolt. They are prebuilt, so they load without being transpiled, and the installer installs the versions each release pins. Package What it does opensec-pi-subagents Specialized agents in separate sessions that inherit the parent's model and thinking level, with parallel workflows and scheduled jobs. opensec-pi-todo A todo list for the model, shown as a live panel above the editor. It survives /reload and compaction. $ pi-bolt install npm:opensec-pi-subagents $ pi-bolt install npm:opensec-pi-todo

title: Extensions
text: Extensions run inside the Pi process with your permissions, whether they are loaded at run time or compiled in. Only install extensions from sources you trust.

title: Integrations
text: Guides Integrations Anything that runs Pi can run Pi-Bolt: it takes the same arguments, speaks the same JSON and RPC protocols, and reads the same configuration. Point the tool at pi-bolt instead of pi .

title: Integrations
text: Agent managers, editors and web interfaces start Pi by running a command, usually pi . Most let you set that command. Set it to pi-bolt , or to the full path that command -v pi-bolt prints. A tool that bundles its own copy of Pi, locked to a version, runs that copy and not Pi-Bolt, unless it lets you choose the Pi executable. Paseo Paseo runs Pi through its pi provider. To run every Pi agent on Pi-Bolt, change that provider's command in ~/.paseo/config.json : { "agents": { "providers": { "pi": { "command": ["pi-bolt"] } } } } Or add Pi-Bolt as a provider of its own, next to Pi. "extends": "pi"

title: Integrations
text: Pi's non-interactive modes work as documented by Pi: $ pi-bolt -p "Summarize the open TODOs" # print mode: answer, then exit $ pi-bolt -p --mode json "Run the tests" # a stream of JSON events $ pi-bolt --mode rpc # controlled by another program over stdio See Pi's CLI , JSON and RPC references. A one-shot pi-bolt -p starts and finishes several times faster than Pi on Bun or Node, which adds up in scripts and CI. Pi's TypeScript SDK embeds Pi in your own program; that program runs on its own runtime, not on Pi-Bolt.

title: Integrations
text: Pi-Bolt runs in tmux, zmx and other multiplexers as Pi does. It also writes less to the terminal: on Linux a session in tmux takes about 28 MB of Pi-Bolt's own memory, against 87 MB for Pi on Bun. See Pi's Run Pi in tmux for tmux settings. If a terminal draws the screen wrongly while the interface scrolls, start Pi-Bolt with PI_TUI_SCROLL_ROWS=0 , which redraws changed rows instead of scrolling them. tmux, zmx, xterm, kitty, Ghostty and VTE terminals do not need it.

title: Integrations
text: Pi-Bolt needs nothing from a Linux image but glibc 2.17 or later. The installer also needs curl or wget , and tar . Install it in the image with PIBOLT_YES=1 , which takes the defaults without asking: RUN curl -fsSL https://pi-bolt.opensec.in/install.sh | PIBOLT_YES=1 sh ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH" Memory limits. Count the executable too: its code is file-backed memory that the kernel charges to the container. Pi-Bolt runs with a limit of about 100 MB, at twice the CPU and with pauses; 256 MB or more leaves it alone. CPU limits. With --cpus , Pi-Bolt starts fewer threads. Address-space l

title: Configuration
text: Guides Configuration Pi-Bolt has no configuration of its own: it reads Pi's. A few environment variables control the Pi-Bolt executable itself, for diagnostics and tuning.

title: Configuration
text: Pi-Bolt and Pi share the agent directory, ~/.pi/agent , and a project's .pi folder: File or folder Holds settings.json Settings: default model, theme, extensions on and off, and more auth.json , models.json Logins and API keys; custom providers and models sessions/ Saved sessions extensions/ , prompts/ Your extensions and prompt templates mcp.json MCP servers Pi's Configuration , Settings and Environment variables pages apply to Pi-Bolt as written. PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR moves the agent directory, and PI_OFFLINE=1 (or --offline ) turns off network operations at startup.

title: Configuration

PIBOLT_HOME npm package: where downloaded builds are kept. Default: ~/.pi-bolt . BUN_AOT=0 Ignore the compiled code and run Pi from bytecode. Use it to tell whether a problem comes from the compiled code. BUN_STATIC_HEAP_VERBOSE=1 Report how the compiled code and prebuilt heap were loaded. PI_TIMING=1 Pi's startup timings, including each extension's factory. PI_TUI_SCROLL_ROWS=0 Redraw every changed row instead of scrolling rows that onl

title: Configuration
text: Pi-Bolt does not read a .env file from the working directory. Pi on Bun does, because Bun loads one into every program's environment; Pi on Node does not. A project's .env (its API keys, its proxy settings) belongs to the project. Set what Pi should see in the shell that starts it.

title: Benchmarks
section: Why a large file write takes so long on stock Pi
text: The 30 seconds are not the disk. A model writes a file by streaming the write tool call's arguments, the whole file, a few characters at a time, so a 200 KB file arrives in thousands of chunks. Stock Pi parses and redraws the whole tool call again for every chunk: each chunk costs more than the last, and the total grows with the square of the file's size. Pi-Bolt processes only the new part of each chunk. In the benchmark the model streams as fast as it can, so the cost shows as wall time. With a real model, which streams more slowly, it shows as CPU: about 40 seconds of it for a 200 KB file o

title: How it works
text: Reference How it works Pi-Bolt does at build time the work that Bun or Node does at every launch: parsing Pi's code, loading its modules and compiling its hot functions. What is left at launch is mapping the result from the executable and running Pi.

title: How it works
text: Stock Pi is JavaScript run by Bun or Node. Every launch, the runtime reads Pi's code, parses it into bytecode, loads and runs every module, and starts Pi in an interpreter. As Pi runs, a JIT compiler watches which functions are hot and what types flow through them, and compiles those to machine code. Until then they are interpreted, and the JIT itself costs CPU, threads and memory.

title: How it works
text: Bundle and compile to bytecode Bun bundles Pi's modules into one program and compiles every function to JavaScriptCore bytecode. Load Pi into a heap Pi's modules are loaded and evaluated, and the resulting heap is saved: the prebuilt heap. It holds Pi's functions, classes and data already set up. Compile every function ahead of time An ahead-of-time compiler turns every function into optimized x86-64 or ARM64 machine code, through B3, the back end of JavaScriptCore's top-tier JIT. Without a running program to watch, it works from what it can prove about the code: whole program type inference,

title: How it works
text: The executable checks that its compiled code fits the engine and the CPU, maps the prebuilt heap and the code from its own file, and runs Pi's main() . Nothing is parsed and nothing is compiled. Pi's modules run their top-level code, as compiled code. If a check fails (an older CPU, a tight address-space limit), the executable says so in one line and runs Pi from bytecode instead: correct, but slower. See Notices at startup .

title: How it works
text: The code and the prebuilt heap are file-backed. Pages that are only read are shared with the system's file cache, and the system can drop them under memory pressure. A process's own memory is what it writes. No JIT in the default build: no compiler threads, no JIT code caches, no profiling data. No bytecode is kept for functions that have machine code.

title: How it works
section: Why it uses less CPU over a session
text: Compiled code accounts for the faster start. Over a session, most of the difference comes from Pi itself: Pi-Bolt carries fixes to Pi's TypeScript where Pi redid work over the whole conversation or the whole streamed output at every step. Examples: a streamed tool call is parsed once, not again for every chunk; a long answer is redrawn incrementally; a command's output is written as it arrives. These fixes are in Pi-Bolt's source, on top of Pi's.

title: How it works
text: Code loaded at run time is not compiled ahead of time. On the default build it is interpreted. Use the JIT build or compile extensions in . No type feedback. A warmed-up JIT specializes on the types it sees; the ahead-of-time compiler uses what it can prove. Code with predictable types gets the fast paths. One executable per Pi release. Each build is made from one Pi release and one engine.

title: How it works
text: The ahead-of-time compiler builds on Jarred Sumner's work for Bun, oven-sh/WebKit#743 . Pi-Bolt ports it to x86-64, macOS on ARM64 and Windows, and adds its own code generation and runtime work. Pi's source with Pi-Bolt's changes is in packages/ of the repository; the engine changes are in patches/ . The full design is in ARCHITECTURE.md .

title: Security
text: Reference Security Every Pi-Bolt release is signed. The installers verify what they download before installing it, need no administrator rights, and change nothing outside your own folders.

title: Security
text: Each release publishes SHA256SUMS , the SHA-256 checksum of every file, and SHA256SUMS.sig , an Ed25519 signature of that file made with Pi-Bolt's release key. The public key is in the repository as keys/release.pub and inside the installers: -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY----- MCowBQYDK2VwAyEAoLboJqtKaoISPqffk03vHZr+1sRBG3uIRIWeKOew+aY= -----END PUBLIC KEY----- The installers and pi-bolt update refuse a download whose checksum or signature does not verify. Checksums and signatures always come from the GitHub release, so a download from the npm registry's CDN is checked against them too.

title: Security
text: $ sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS $ openssl pkeyutl -verify -pubin -inkey release.pub -rawin -in SHA256SUMS -sigfile SHA256SUMS.sig The second command needs OpenSSL 3 or later; macOS's own openssl (LibreSSL) cannot check Ed25519, but Homebrew's openssl@3 can.

title: Security
text: Installs into your home folder ( ~/.pi-bolt , or %USERPROFILE%\.pi-bolt on Windows) and links one command. It needs no administrator rights and changes no security setting. On Windows, asks before adding Pi-Bolt to your PATH. Installs OpenSec's optional extensions only when you say yes, at the versions the release pins, and only if the registry's package matches the pinned integrity hash. Does not touch your Pi installation. In ~/.pi/agent it only installs the extensions you accepted.

title: Security
text: Pi-Bolt runs Pi's tools with your permissions, as Pi does: the agent can read and write files and run commands in your project. Pi's Run Pi safely and Isolate Pi apply to Pi-Bolt. Extensions run inside the Pi process with your permissions. Only install extensions from sources you trust. A project's .env is not loaded into Pi-Bolt's environment. See .env files . Crash reports contain an encoded stack trace and nothing else: no file names, paths or data of yours. See A crash .

title: Security
text: Report security issues privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting , not in public issues. We acknowledge the report, investigate, and coordinate a fix and disclosure with you. In scope: the Pi-Bolt runtime and engine changes, the release executables, and the scripts and installers in the repository. Vulnerabilities in Pi itself belong to Pi ; vulnerabilities in Bun or JavaScriptCore that Pi-Bolt does not change belong to their projects.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Help Troubleshooting Most problems are a PATH, a platform requirement or an extension. Start by checking that Pi-Bolt runs its compiled code, then find your symptom below.

title: Troubleshooting
text: $ BUN_STATIC_HEAP_VERBOSE=1 pi-bolt --version [aot] image of 42467328 bytes mapped, 35635200 of them code [static heap] 94109736 bytes in executable, mapped: true [aot] image registered: true 1.1.0 (Pi-Bolt 0.8.0, linux-x64, JIT off) image registered: true means Pi runs its ahead-of-time compiled code. Without the variable, a healthy executable prints nothing extra.

text: When the compiled code cannot be used, Pi-Bolt prints one line and runs Pi from bytecode. text: Killed at once ( zsh: killed ), or "cannot verify the developer" The executable is quarantined: it was downloaded with a browser. Install with the installer or npm, which do not quarantine, or remove the attribute: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine pi-bolt-darwin-arm64 . "Pi-Bolt runs on Macs with Apple silicon only" There is no build for Intel Macs. text: First, check whether the problem is Pi-Bolt's: If it also happens with BUN_AOT=0 pi-bolt and with stock Pi, it is Pi's: report it to Pi . title: FAQ
text: Is Pi-Bolt a replacement for Pi, or an add-on? It is a complete Pi in one executable: you do not need Pi, Node.js or Bun installed. If you have Pi, Pi-Bolt runs next to it as pi-bolt and uses the same configuration, sessions and extensions. Is it a rewrite of Pi? No. Pi-Bolt is Pi's own TypeScript source, compiled ahead of time to native code, with a small set of fixes on top. That is why Pi's behavior, commands and extensions carry over. See How it works . title: FAQ
text: Why is the JIT off by default? Pi is already compiled to machine code, so a JIT would only add compiler threads, warm-up and memory. The JIT only helps code loaded at run time, such as heavy extensions. For those, install the JIT build: it keeps nearly all of Pi-Bolt's gains, within about 5%. See Choose a build . Why does stock Pi take 30 seconds to write a 200 KB file? It is not the disk. The file arrives as a streamed tool call in thousands of small chunks, and stock Pi parses and redraws the whole call for each one, so the work grows with the square of the file's size. title: FAQ
text: Do my extensions work? Yes, unchanged. Extensions that use bun:ffi , such as pi-fff, need the JIT build. Extensions that start Pi themselves may need to be pointed at pi-bolt . See Extensions . Does it work with Paseo and other tools that run Pi? Yes. Set the tool's Pi command to pi-bolt . See Integrations . Does codemode work? Yes. Codemode is built into Pi and runs in Pi-Bolt as it does in Pi: pi-bolt -t +codemode .

title: FAQ
text: Which platforms are supported? macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon, Linux on x86-64 with glibc 2.17 or later, and Windows 10 (1809) or later on x64. See Requirements . Does it run on Linux ARM64, or on Android? Not yet. There is no Linux ARM64 build, and Android uses a different C library from the glibc that the Linux build needs. Is it free? Yes. Pi-Bolt is MIT licensed. Release executables include Bun (MIT), JavaScriptCore (LGPL-2.0 and BSD), ICU and Pi (MIT); see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md .
